newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Nov 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Nov 11.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
-- BANKS FACE PROBE OVER EUROTUNNEL SHARE DEALS

The Senior Fraud Office, at the request of the French police, is to launch an investigation into whether or not banks and brokerages in London have been involved in illegal manipulation of the market for shares in Eurotunnel. The company itself revealed that it believed the investigation related specifically to share movements prior to a 1994 rights issue. In the past the COB, the French bourse regulatory body, has expressed suspicion about share movements.
-- PRU APPOINTS HEAD OF EQUITY INVESTMENT

It is reported that Nick Mustoe will be named by Prudential Corp on Monday as the new head of UK equities at its investment management division. Formerly with UBS unit PDFM, Mustoe will head British equities at Prudential Portfolio Managers - a unit with 88.6 billion stg under management. He will also join PPM's management committee.
-- LABOUR TO REASSURE BUSINESS ON EU POWERS

In an effort to reassure British business leaders Labour will on Monday give an assurance that it would resist any extension of the EU's majority voting powers on its social chapter. British companies have expressed concern about the impact on costs and bureaucracy of additional regulation. A poll for the Confederation of British Industry has found that 73 percent of business leaders are keen to see the country's opt-out on the social chapter maintained.
-- BRUSSELS CHALLENGE OVER LOAN GUARANTEES

The European Commission is reported to be considering outlawing the provision of loan guarantees by member governments to financially troubled companies. Some observers see the provision of such guarantees as simply another less obvious way of providing state subsidy. There is reported to be considerable unease within the banking community at the prospect of having thousands of loans made to ailing companies rendered illegal.
-- INITIATIVE ON FREE TRADE UNDERMINED BY LEAK

There is concern that a government white paper to be launched on the issue of free trade policy, attempting to raise the country's position of champion of free markets, will have been undermined by the leaking of a Downing Street memorandum which admits that very little in the document is in fact new. The memo on the joint initiative from the foreign office and the department of trade and industry notes that presentation will be crucial if it is to have the desired impact.
-- US UTILITY NEAR DECISION ON 1.2 BILLION STG EAST MIDLANDS BID

US power company Dominion Resources is reported to be on the verge of deciding whether or not to go ahead with a takeover bid for East Midlands Electricity, the UK regional electricity company. An offer valuing the company at 1.29 billion stg, or 650 pence a share, could be made by as soon as Monday morning following a series of weekend meetings of executives of the Virginia-based company.
-- TORIES CRITICISED FOR FAILING TO INVEST IN LONDON

A report from the London Pride Partnership has accused the government of undermining the position of London as a world capital by failing to invest sufficiently in the city. The report in particular highlights the poor state of the capital's transport infrastructure and dilapidated state of repair of many of its parks and buildings. Copies of the report will eventually be sent to the three major political parties.
-- NEW TACTICS FOR EU TRADE

European Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan in a personal commentary discusses why he believes it to be in the best interests of Europe as a whole for the European Commission to be accorded sole negotiating rights in talks aimed at securing increased international trade liberalisation. He warns that unless such an approach is adopted the EU risks throwing away considerable gains already made in this area.
-- MINISTERS TO SEEK PACT ON EMU BUDGET DEFICIT RULES

A meeting takes place on Monday of EU finance ministers at which further attempts will be made at securing agreement on a stability pact covering continued budgetary discipline among EU member states participating in the single currency. Germany is insistent that rigid rules applied in this area, with automatic sanctions for those countries that allow discipline in this area to ease. A considerably less rigidly defined pact is being sought by states such as Britain and Spain.
